comment: AQA GCSE Geography 8035 multiple choice — Paper 2 Challenges in the Human Environment: Section A urban issues (module 08), Section B the changing economic world (module 09), Section C resource management and the energy option (module 10). Definitions, case study figures and processes, all taken from the Dulwich College material: the Case Study Summary Booklet 2026, the topic revision mats, the AQA List of Key Terms and the June 2019–2025 Paper 2 question papers and mark schemes. Four options, answer is the 0-based index of the correct one.

08-urban-issues-and-challenges.q: Urbanisation is best defined as…
options: the increase in the proportion of a population living in towns and cities
the absolute increase in the size of a city
the movement of people from one country to another
the spread of a city into the surrounding countryside
08-urban-issues-and-challenges.explain: Urbanisation is a proportion. An absolute increase in city size is urban growth, and spread into the countryside is urban sprawl — AQA asked for this exact definition for 1 mark in 2025.

08-urban-issues-and-challenges.q: A megacity is an urban area with a population of at least…
08-urban-issues-and-challenges.explain: AQA's own wording is "in excess of ten million people". There were 33 megacities in 2023 and around 50 are expected by 2050.

08-urban-issues-and-challenges.q: What proportion of the world's increased urban population is expected to be in Africa and Asia?
08-urban-issues-and-challenges.explain: 90% — one of the school's own recall facts. It is why the LIC/NEE city case study carries so much of Section A.

08-urban-issues-and-challenges.q: Which region is the most urbanised in the world?
08-urban-issues-and-challenges.explain: North America is the most urbanised region, with roughly 82% of its population in urban areas; HICs generally are at least 75% urban.

08-urban-issues-and-challenges.q: Which three countries are expected to account for 37% of the growth in the world's urban population between 2014 and 2050?
08-urban-issues-and-challenges.explain: India, China and Nigeria. The combination of huge populations and rapid rural–urban migration concentrates global urban growth in these three.

08-urban-issues-and-challenges.q: The two factors that affect the rate of urbanisation are…
08-urban-issues-and-challenges.explain: Migration and natural increase. They are linked: migrants are typically aged 18–35, so the birth rate rises and the death rate stays low.

08-urban-issues-and-challenges.q: Rio de Janeiro has grown up around which feature?
options: Guanabara Bay, a large natural bay
08-urban-issues-and-challenges.explain: Guanabara Bay in south-east Brazil. The bay is also where the city's water pollution problem concentrates — 150 tonnes a day.

08-urban-issues-and-challenges.q: Roughly how many people live in the Greater Rio de Janeiro metropolitan area?
08-urban-issues-and-challenges.explain: 13 million in Greater Rio, of whom around 1.5 million live in favelas — about 24% of the city, across roughly 1,000 favelas.

08-urban-issues-and-challenges.q: Rio de Janeiro's national importance includes which figure?
options: 22% of Brazil's GNI and the largest port in Brazil
5% of Brazil's GNI and the 3rd busiest port in Brazil
08-urban-issues-and-challenges.explain: 5% of Brazil's GNI and the third busiest port. It is also Brazil's second most important industrial centre — and Brasília, not Rio, is the capital.

08-urban-issues-and-challenges.q: Infant mortality in the Cidade de Deus favela compared with the wealthy district of Barra is…
08-urban-issues-and-challenges.explain: 21 per 1,000 in Cidade de Deus against 9 in Barra. Favela residents also live about 13 years less than people in wealthier parts of Rio.

08-urban-issues-and-challenges.q: What percentage of children in Rio continue in education beyond the age of 14?
08-urban-issues-and-challenges.explain: Only about 50%, despite Rio having over 400 secondary schools, 6 universities and a 97% literacy rate — the classic "opportunity exists but is unevenly shared" contrast.

08-urban-issues-and-challenges.q: The Guandu water treatment plant in Rio is notable because it is…
options: the largest water treatment plant in the world
08-urban-issues-and-challenges.explain: The world's largest, supplying the great majority of Rio's fresh water — yet 12% of favela homes still lack running water and a third of supply is lost to leaks, fraud and illegal access.

08-urban-issues-and-challenges.q: Which scheme supplies around 30% of Rio's energy?
08-urban-issues-and-challenges.explain: The Simplício HEP plant, built at a cost of $2 billion and opened in 2013, supplies about 30% of Rio's energy.

08-urban-issues-and-challenges.q: Roughly how many people work in Rio's informal economy, and for about how much?
08-urban-issues-and-challenges.explain: 3.5 million people on about £75 a month. Informal workers pay no tax, which starves the city of revenue — the key disadvantage of the informal economy.

08-urban-issues-and-challenges.q: Air pollution caused largely by congestion in Rio causes approximately how many deaths a year?
08-urban-issues-and-challenges.explain: About 5,000 a year. Rio is the most congested city in South America and car ownership rose 40% in ten years — an environmental challenge affecting the whole city, not just the favelas.

08-urban-issues-and-challenges.q: What proportion of Rio's waste is recycled?
08-urban-issues-and-challenges.explain: Less than 2%. Most goes to the Seropédica landfill 70 km away, where landfill gas is captured to generate electricity or fuel the collection vehicles.

08-urban-issues-and-challenges.q: The Favela-Bairro Project ran from…
08-urban-issues-and-challenges.explain: 1995–2009, a site and service scheme costing the government $1 billion and helping 250,000 people across more than 100 favelas.

08-urban-issues-and-challenges.q: Which measure is usually identified as the most important thing the Favela-Bairro Project did?
options: Giving residents legal ownership of the land they lived on
Building the Complexo do Alemão cable car
08-urban-issues-and-challenges.explain: Legal land title, plus 100% mortgages and low-interest loans, gave residents a reason to invest in homes they could no longer be evicted from — so they rebuilt in brick.

08-urban-issues-and-challenges.q: Before the Favela-Bairro Project, what proportion of non-improved favelas had no sewage connection?
08-urban-issues-and-challenges.explain: 50% had no sewage connection and 30% had no electricity. The project built 12 new sewage works and installed 60 km of new power cables.

08-urban-issues-and-challenges.q: A criticism of the Favela-Bairro Project is that…
options: it demolished favelas rather than upgrading them
funding was reduced after 2008, so long-term sustainability is doubtful
it refused to give residents legal land title
it was funded entirely by foreign TNCs
08-urban-issues-and-challenges.explain: Funding fell after 2008; improvements were also uneven with some favelas left out, pacification displaced residents, and some new pavements raised flood risk on steep slopes.

08-urban-issues-and-challenges.q: What percentage of London's population was born outside the UK?
08-urban-issues-and-challenges.explain: 37%. London's migrant streams were dominated by the former British Empire after WWII and by Eastern Europe after EU free movement in 2007.

08-urban-issues-and-challenges.q: London generates approximately what share of the UK's GNI?
08-urban-issues-and-challenges.explain: 22% of UK GNI. Average earnings are also about £6,000 a year higher in London, and the city attracts 30 million tourists a year through 6 major airports.

08-urban-issues-and-challenges.q: The life expectancy gap between Chelsea and Tower Hamlets is…
08-urban-issues-and-challenges.explain: 88 in Chelsea against 80 in Tower Hamlets, which also has the highest poverty rate of any London borough at 56%.

08-urban-issues-and-challenges.q: London's homeless population of around 170,000 represents roughly what share of the UK total?
08-urban-issues-and-challenges.explain: About half the UK total. Average house prices are over £500,000 and rough sleeping has risen 23% since 2020.

08-urban-issues-and-challenges.q: A brownfield site is best defined as…
options: land that has been used, abandoned and now awaits some new use
land on the rural–urban fringe that has never been built on
any derelict building in a city centre
08-urban-issues-and-challenges.explain: AQA's wording exactly, and it is commonly found in the inner city. London had almost 3,000 brownfield sites covering 2,600 hectares in 2019.

08-urban-issues-and-challenges.q: Before regeneration, Stratford in east London was notable as…
options: London's largest area of greenfield land
the most polluted site in Western Europe
the borough with the highest house prices
the site of London's main container port
08-urban-issues-and-challenges.explain: The most polluted site in Western Europe, with derelict industries, poor transport links and one of the most deprived communities in the country.

08-urban-issues-and-challenges.q: How much green space does the Queen Elizabeth Olympic Park contain?
08-urban-issues-and-challenges.explain: 100 hectares of green space within the 250-hectare park. The International Quarter holds 25,000 workers and over 20,000 jobs are expected by 2030, bringing more than £5 billion.

08-urban-issues-and-challenges.q: East Village in Stratford reduces water consumption by roughly how much compared with the average?
08-urban-issues-and-challenges.explain: 50% less water, through rainwater harvesting and grey water recycling, and 30% less energy from a biomass Combined Heat and Power system. 99% is the parkland waste recycling figure.

08-urban-issues-and-challenges.q: CHP, used at East Village, stands for…
08-urban-issues-and-challenges.explain: Combined Heat and Power generates electricity and useful heat simultaneously, so far less energy is wasted than in a conventional power station.

08-urban-issues-and-challenges.q: By how much did NO₂ levels fall in London's original ULEZ zone?
08-urban-issues-and-challenges.explain: 44%. The Congestion Charge figure is a 30% fall in central traffic since 2003, and 66% is the share of London's waste sent to incineration in 2021.

09-the-changing-economic-world.q: Which measure of development combines income, life expectancy and education levels?
09-the-changing-economic-world.explain: HDI combines GDP per capita, life expectancy and adult literacy into a single index. AQA asked this for 1 mark in 2023.

09-the-changing-economic-world.q: Gross national income (GNI) differs from GDP because it also includes…
09-the-changing-economic-world.explain: GNI takes into account not just goods and services but income earned from investments overseas, then divides by population.

09-the-changing-economic-world.q: The main limitation of every economic and social measure of development is that…
options: they cannot be compared between countries
the data is always out of date
they are averages for the whole country, so they hide internal inequality
09-the-changing-economic-world.explain: Averages describe nobody: Nigeria's GDP per head is US$3,617 in the south and US$292 in its poorest region. This is the reason examiners want for any "limitations" question.

09-the-changing-economic-world.q: Why can an HIC have a higher death rate than an LIC?
options: Death rate depends on age structure, and HICs have far more elderly people
09-the-changing-economic-world.explain: A crude death rate reflects age structure: Japan has 28% over 65, so its death rate is high even though life expectancy is among the world's highest. Infant mortality is the better health indicator.

09-the-changing-economic-world.q: Infant mortality in Nigeria and the UK is approximately…
09-the-changing-economic-world.explain: 94 against 5. Life expectancy is 54 against 81, internet users 47% against 93%, and HDI rank 164th against 13th.

09-the-changing-economic-world.q: Which stage of the Demographic Transition Model is Japan in?
09-the-changing-economic-world.explain: Stage 5: the death rate slightly exceeds the birth rate, so the population falls and ages. In 2020 Japan had 12% under 15 and 28% over 65.

09-the-changing-economic-world.q: In Stage 2 of the DTM, population rises rapidly because…
options: the death rate falls while the birth rate stays high
09-the-changing-economic-world.explain: Clean water, better food supply and basic medicine cut deaths, but attitudes to family size have not yet changed — so births greatly exceed deaths.

09-the-changing-economic-world.q: The economic benefit of Stage 3 is that…
options: the total population finally stops growing
the working-age population grows relative to dependents
the death rate falls below the birth rate
09-the-changing-economic-world.explain: The demographic dividend: the large Stage 2 cohort reaches working age as the birth rate falls, so there are more workers and fewer dependents, more women in paid work, and more income available to save, invest or tax.

09-the-changing-economic-world.q: Which of these is a PHYSICAL cause of uneven development?
options: Being landlocked, so there is no port for trade
09-the-changing-economic-world.explain: Physical causes are weather and climate, relief, being landlocked, tropical disease environments and water shortages. Trade is economic and colonialism historical.

09-the-changing-economic-world.q: How many people died of malaria in 2019?
09-the-changing-economic-world.explain: 400,000, almost all in LICs — the standard figure for disparities in health as a consequence of uneven development.

09-the-changing-economic-world.q: What share of global wealth is held in North America?
09-the-changing-economic-world.explain: 34% of global wealth in a region with a small fraction of the world's people — the headline figure for disparities in wealth.

09-the-changing-economic-world.q: Debt relief reduces the development gap by…
options: cancelling money already owed, so repayments can fund development instead
lending money at a lower rate of interest
giving goods and services rather than cash
guaranteeing a fair price for exports
09-the-changing-economic-world.explain: Cancellation, not lending — the 2023 examiner's report says candidates routinely conflated debt relief with loans. $75 billion was written off across the 19 HIPCs.

09-the-changing-economic-world.q: Total debt relief across the 19 Heavily Indebted Poor Countries amounted to…
09-the-changing-economic-world.explain: $75 billion. $12.5 billion is the Grameen Bank's total lending and $34 billion is Peru's projected earnings from Camisea.

09-the-changing-economic-world.q: Intermediate technology is best described as…
options: simple, easily learned and maintained technology serving local needs
technology halfway between manual and automated
09-the-changing-economic-world.explain: AQA's definition. The point is that it can be repaired locally without imported parts or outside expertise — which is why Chambamontera's micro-hydro scheme is sustainable.

09-the-changing-economic-world.q: What proportion of small coffee farmers in eastern Uganda have joined the Gumutindo Co-operative?
09-the-changing-economic-world.explain: 90%. Collective organisation gives Fairtrade farmers the scale to negotiate and export directly, on top of the guaranteed price and the community premium.

09-the-changing-economic-world.q: Tourism contributed approximately what share of Jamaica's GDP in 2019?
09-the-changing-economic-world.explain: 35% of GDP, from 4 million visitors a year, generating about $2 billion and over 50% of Jamaica's total foreign exchange earnings.

09-the-changing-economic-world.q: Roughly how many Jamaicans are employed directly and indirectly in tourism?
09-the-changing-economic-world.explain: Over 200,000 — tourism is the country's main source of employment and its second largest employer.

09-the-changing-economic-world.q: Which of these is a genuine limitation of tourism-led development in Jamaica?
options: Visitor numbers have fallen every year since 1994
The government banned cruise ships at Falmouth
Wealthy areas such as Montego Bay have benefited most, and pockets of poverty persist
09-the-changing-economic-world.explain: The benefits are geographically concentrated, and roads for residents came late because ports and airports were prioritised. Growth in arrivals also slowed in 2009 because of the recession abroad.

09-the-changing-economic-world.q: Nigeria borders which group of countries?
09-the-changing-economic-world.explain: Benin, Niger, Chad and Cameroon, with the Gulf of Guinea to the south. It is in West Africa.

09-the-changing-economic-world.q: Nigeria became independent of the UK in…
09-the-changing-economic-world.explain: 1960. Its political and trading links ran almost entirely to the UK before that; it now trades most with the EU, USA and India, with links to China growing.

09-the-changing-economic-world.q: Oil accounts for what share of Nigeria's GDP and export earnings respectively?
09-the-changing-economic-world.explain: 14% of GDP but 98% of export earnings — which is why the whole economy is exposed to the world oil price despite oil being a small part of domestic activity.

09-the-changing-economic-world.q: Nigeria's service sector now accounts for roughly what share of its economy?
09-the-changing-economic-world.explain: 53%, with manufacturing at 27% and growing fastest. Employment in agriculture has fallen by 40% through mechanisation and better pay elsewhere.

09-the-changing-economic-world.q: Shell began operating in Nigeria in…
09-the-changing-economic-world.explain: 1958, with the discovery of oil and controversial extraction operations in the Niger Delta.

09-the-changing-economic-world.q: Which of these is an ADVANTAGE of Shell to Nigeria?
options: Oil spills at Bodo cleaned the Niger Delta
Around 90% of its contracts are awarded to Nigerian companies
09-the-changing-economic-world.explain: Around 90% of contracts to local firms (AQA's 2025 scheme gives 91%), plus $250,000 on healthcare and 3,000 school scholarships. Bermuda registration is a disadvantage, because less tax is paid.

09-the-changing-economic-world.q: How many residents took out a lawsuit against Shell over oil pollution in Ogoniland?
09-the-changing-economic-world.explain: 42,000. Contamination in Ogoniland is 1,000 times higher than elsewhere, following two massive spills at Bodo in the Niger Delta.

09-the-changing-economic-world.q: What percentage of Nigeria's forests have been destroyed by logging, agriculture and urban expansion?
09-the-changing-economic-world.explain: 96%. 94% is the share of the population exposed to high air pollution, and 60% is the share living in poverty.

09-the-changing-economic-world.q: Between 1990 and 2019, Nigeria's access to safe water rose from…
09-the-changing-economic-world.explain: 46% to 85% — paired with a 9-year rise in life expectancy between 2015 and 2019, these are the quality-of-life gains that stop a Nigeria answer being one-sided.

09-the-changing-economic-world.q: De-industrialisation is defined as the decline of traditional manufacturing due to…
options: exhaustion of raw materials, loss of markets and competition from NEEs
09-the-changing-economic-world.explain: AQA's own definition. In the UK it meant the decline of coal mining, shipbuilding and steel, with a negative multiplier effect as suppliers closed too — North East England was worst hit.

09-the-changing-economic-world.q: Approximately what share of the UK economy comes from the tertiary sector?
09-the-changing-economic-world.explain: 80% tertiary, with 1.7% from research. 1.3 million people work in IT, and digital technology turnover grew 2.6 times faster than UK GDP in 2016–17.

09-the-changing-economic-world.q: Torr Quarry in Somerset contributes how much a year to the local economy, and how much land has been landscaped?
09-the-changing-economic-world.explain: £15 million a year and 80 hectares landscaped, with the Somerset Wildlife Trust creating biodiverse-rich landscapes. 2.5 km² is the size of the quarry itself.

10-resource-management.q: In Section C of Paper 2, which questions should you answer?
options: Question 03 and one of Questions 04, 05 or 06
10-resource-management.explain: Question 03 is compulsory, then one option: 04 Food, 05 Water or 06 Energy. Your class does Energy — and Q03 covers UK food, water AND energy regardless.

10-resource-management.q: Resource management is defined as…
options: the extraction of resources for profit
the control and monitoring of resources so they do not become depleted or exhausted
the transfer of resources between countries
reducing the use of non-renewable resources to zero
10-resource-management.explain: AQA's wording. A resource itself is "something which human society attaches value to due to its usefulness".

10-resource-management.q: Which regions are described as prone to water shortages and drought?
options: Europe, South East Asia and northern North America
Africa, the Middle East and Australia
10-resource-management.explain: Africa, the Middle East and Australia. Europe, South East Asia, northern South America and northern North America have a water surplus.

10-resource-management.q: Roughly how many countries face food insecurity?
10-resource-management.explain: About 50 countries, and more than 800 million people live every day with hunger or food insecurity. The food deficit regions are sub-Saharan Africa plus India, Pakistan, Bangladesh and Afghanistan.

10-resource-management.q: What percentage of the food eaten in the UK comes from LICs?
10-resource-management.explain: 12% — which raises food miles and the carbon footprint of the UK diet. Coincidentally, 12% of UK greenhouse gas emissions also come from agriculture itself.

10-resource-management.q: Food miles means…
options: the distance covered supplying food to consumers
the distance a farmer travels to market
the carbon emitted per kilogram of food
the area of land needed to feed one person
10-resource-management.explain: AQA's definition. Local food sourcing cuts food miles — but out-of-season UK produce grown in heated glasshouses can still have a high footprint.

10-resource-management.q: Organic produce is defined partly by the fact that…
options: it is always grown within 50 miles of the consumer
artificial fertilisers are banned and fertility is built by crop rotation, compost, manure and clover
it uses hydroponics rather than soil
it is grown only in greenhouses
10-resource-management.explain: No artificial fertilisers and no synthetic additives such as pesticides and dyes; soil fertility comes from rotation, compost, manure and clover.

10-resource-management.q: Agribusiness increases food production mainly because…
options: it relies on hand labour rather than machines
it reduces the amount of land farmed
farming takes place on a greater scale, with hedgerows removed and more mechanisation and chemicals
10-resource-management.explain: Larger farms created by combining fields and removing hedgerows, with greater use of mechanisation and chemicals to raise yields — at the cost of habitat and chemical runoff.

10-resource-management.q: Why does the UK need water transfer schemes even though it receives enough rainfall overall?
options: Rainfall is greatest in the west while demand is greatest in the drier south-east
Rainfall has declined every year since 1990
All UK rainfall falls in winter
The UK exports most of its water
10-resource-management.explain: A spatial mismatch: the wettest region is the west, the highest demand is in the south-east, which is also the driest and runs a water deficit — so water is transferred between river basins.

10-resource-management.q: Average daily water consumption per person in the UK is about…
10-resource-management.explain: 310 litres a day, and demand is expected to exceed supply by 2034. Dishwasher ownership rose from 22% in 1998 to 49% in 2018.

10-resource-management.q: Eutrophication in UK rivers is caused by…
options: oil and heavy metals from transport
nutrients from fertiliser and sewage producing algae that reduce oxygen levels
plastic microbeads blocking the river bed
warm water discharged from power stations
10-resource-management.explain: Nutrients from farmland and sewage feed algal growth, which depletes dissolved oxygen and kills fish — causing economic losses to fishermen and tourism.

10-resource-management.q: What proportion of UK energy was 'green' in 2020?
10-resource-management.explain: 47% in 2020. 35% was the share imported in 2019, and 65% is the renewables target for 2030.

10-resource-management.q: Which statement best describes the UK's changing energy mix?
options: A shift from fossil fuels and nuclear towards renewables, with nuclear falling only slightly
A shift from renewables back to gas
A shift from nuclear to coal
No significant change in the last 30 years
10-resource-management.explain: Fossil fuel use has fallen because of environmental impact and declining domestic supplies; renewables have risen for environmental benefit and carbon targets; nuclear has fallen slightly.

10-resource-management.q: Approximately how much does a new nuclear power station cost to build?
10-resource-management.explain: About £22 billion, against roughly £4 million for a commercial wind turbine — high set-up costs are the main economic barrier to new low-carbon capacity.

10-resource-management.q: Energy security is defined as…
options: the uninterrupted availability of energy sources at an affordable price
generating all of a country's energy domestically
having enough fossil fuel reserves to last 50 years
having no power cuts in a given year
10-resource-management.explain: Both halves matter — uninterrupted AND affordable — which is why an HIC with plenty of supply can still be insecure when prices spike.

10-resource-management.q: Energy insecurity is best defined as…
options: an energy deficit, where demand exceeds supply
when energy availability is not enough to ensure good health, livelihood and earnings
the absence of any renewable generation
importing more than half of a country's energy
10-resource-management.explain: AQA's wording. The 2023 examiner's report notes the only common error was candidates defining an energy DEFICIT instead.

10-resource-management.q: Which of these are the three drivers of rising global energy consumption?
options: Economic development, rising population and technology
10-resource-management.explain: Economic development, population growth and technology. GNI per person and energy consumption per person are positively correlated across the world's countries.

10-resource-management.q: What share of the world's unexploited natural gas is thought to lie in the Arctic?
10-resource-management.explain: 30% — which is why the Arctic is becoming politically contested as the ice retreats, linking energy insecurity to conflict and to risk in a sensitive environment.

10-resource-management.q: Which of these is NOT one of the four factors affecting energy supply named by the specification?
10-resource-management.explain: The four are physical factors, cost of exploitation and production, technology, and political factors. Population affects demand, not supply.

10-resource-management.q: What makes tidal power fundamentally different from wind and solar?
options: It is predictable, because tidal cycles are known years in advance
It can be built anywhere on a coast
10-resource-management.explain: Predictability. Wind and solar are intermittent and so need backup capacity; tides are astronomical and can be planned into the grid. The 2023 report says understanding reliability separated the best answers.

10-resource-management.q: Which renewable source is described as effectively constant, 24 hours a day?
10-resource-management.explain: Geothermal, generated by heat stored deep in the Earth, with a tiny surface footprint — but only economic where hot rock is near the surface, so geographically very restricted.

10-resource-management.q: By how much has Brazil reduced its petrol consumption by introducing bio-ethanol?
10-resource-management.explain: 40%. Biomass uses recently absorbed carbon and can use waste, but monoculture for biofuel reduces biodiversity and competes with food crops for land.

10-resource-management.q: A disadvantage of hydro-electric power in upland areas is that…
options: large areas of land are flooded behind the dam
it produces greenhouse gases while generating
10-resource-management.explain: Flooding valleys displaces people and drowns habitat. HEP's advantage is that it is reliable and output can be raised within minutes to match demand.

10-resource-management.q: The Camisea project in Peru extracts which fossil fuel?
10-resource-management.explain: Natural gas, from the Camisea region of the Peruvian Amazon, piped across the Andes to the coast. Gas is the cleanest fossil fuel, with 45% less CO₂.

10-resource-management.q: How much could Peru earn from Camisea exports over the project's life?
10-resource-management.explain: US$34 billion over the 30-year life. US$4 billion is the separate saving in Peru's own energy costs; US$51,000 is the Chambamontera community's contribution.

10-resource-management.q: Which is a disadvantage of the Camisea project?
options: Clearing routes for the pipelines has led to landslides
It uses more CO₂-intensive fuel than coal
10-resource-management.explain: Removing forest removes the roots binding steep Andean slopes. Other disadvantages: deforestation destroying habitat, impacts on indigenous tribes who may lack immunity to developers' diseases, and controversial fracking.

10-resource-management.q: The Chambamontera scheme in Peru is…
options: a micro-hydro scheme in the Andes
a solar farm on the coast
10-resource-management.explain: A micro-hydro scheme in the Andes mountains, supported by the charity Practical Action, built because isolated communities are cut off from the main electricity network.

10-resource-management.q: How much did the Chambamontera community contribute to the cost of its scheme?
options: Nothing — it was fully funded by Practical Action
US$510,000 in total, about $7,500 per family
US$5,100 in total, about $75 per family
US$51,000 in total, about $750 per family
10-resource-management.explain: US$51,000, about $750 per family. Paying for it gives the community ownership and the incentive to maintain it — the logic of intermediate technology.

10-resource-management.q: Which outcome of the Chambamontera scheme is specifically recorded?
options: A new road to the nearest city
Electric street lighting, improving quality of life and economic opportunities
A hospital built by the Peruvian government
10-resource-management.explain: Reliable electricity and electric street lighting, alongside renewable generation, low environmental impact, and low maintenance and running costs.

10-resource-management.q: A sustainable energy supply is defined by AQA as the combination of…
options: energy savings, efficiency measures and technologies, and renewable energy sources
imported energy and domestic fossil fuels
10-resource-management.explain: Savings are listed first, which is why energy conservation counts as a way of achieving a sustainable supply even though it generates nothing — reducing demand moves the supply-demand balance exactly as new capacity would.
